title: Finding People to Teach
focus: Practice topic: sharing the gospel in a natural way
intro: The Lord prepares people to hear the gospel, and He asks members and missionaries to find them together. In this lesson learners build the faith to find, learn how members help, and use every tool God has given, including the internet.
preparation: Study Doctrine and Covenants 18:10, 14–16; 33:6–11; 88:81; and 100:5–6. Study Alma 31:34–35. Prepare to show short videos on finding people to teach, a member-missionary story and sharing beliefs online. Ask one or two learners to demonstrate how to start a gospel conversation. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: The faith to find
paras: Tell the story of Wilford Woodruff in England soon after he became an Apostle. He prayed to know where to go. He felt led to the south of England and to the farm of John Benbow, where many people had already been preparing. Many were baptized. Ask: What did Elder Woodruff do to find people? How did the Lord help him?

Draw out the truth: when we act in faith, the Lord prepares people for us. Ask how that thought changes how a missionary feels about finding people. Read Alma 31:34–35 and ask what Alma prayed for before he taught the Zoramites. Ask why we should act on the feelings to reach out.

sections.title: A family of God
paras: Read what the missionary manual says about the family of God. Ask how knowing that every person is a child of God changes how we feel about finding people.

Ask what challenges missionaries face when finding people to teach. Remind learners that the Lord sends the Holy Ghost to guide them, and ask what He would have missionaries do when people do not respond. Read Doctrine and Covenants 18:10, 14–16 and ask what these verses teach about the worth of souls.

sections.title: Members and missionaries together
paras: Share how President Thomas S. Monson called on members and missionaries to work together. Read Doctrine and Covenants 88:81. Ask why “now” is the time to work together.

Ask what can happen when members and missionaries serve together. Show the video of a family helped by members. Ask what efforts led to their blessings, and what moved those members to reach out. Read the section on how no effort is wasted. Ask why no effort to share the gospel is wasted even if a person does not accept it, and how a missionary stays hopeful.

sections.title: Taking part in member missionary work
paras: Write these scriptures on the board: Doctrine and Covenants 18:10, 14–16; 33:6–11; 100:5–6. Each learner reads one and tells the class what blessings are promised to those who share the gospel.

Write this idea on the board: as member missionaries, we find people when we pray, act and trust the Lord. Share Elder M. Russell Ballard’s counsel to pray for opportunities, personally and as a family, and to trust the Lord’s promise that He will give words in the very moment (see Doctrine and Covenants 100:5–6). Let learners search the list of ideas for helping others learn the gospel and pick one or two they can do now. Ask why some members hesitate, and how to move past the fear.

sections.title: Using every tool
paras: Share Elder L. Tom Perry’s counsel that the way we find people is changing, because the Lord has opened the internet to missionary work. Ask why members and missionaries should use online tools.

Read the Church’s guidelines for using social media. Ask what each one means for a missionary. Show a short video on sharing beliefs. Ask how technology can help members share the gospel, and invite learners to say how they could use it to share a testimony. Close with testimony.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Show the faith to find
examples.text: Tell the Woodruff and Benbow story in two minutes. Show what he did first, which was pray.

examples.title: Show how members help
examples.text: Read Doctrine and Covenants 88:81. Explain what the Lord asks of those who have received the gospel.

examples.title: Show a safe first step
examples.text: Name three simple ways to start a gospel conversation, such as sharing a thought, offering help and inviting to an event.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Start a gospel conversation
examples.text: Show a warm, natural way to ask a neighbor about faith and family. Keep it short and kind.

examples.title: Invite someone to meet missionaries
examples.text: Show how to invite a friend to learn more, using your own testimony.

examples.title: Share a post online
examples.text: Show how to share a short message and your feelings on social media, following the guidelines.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Start a conversation in pairs
examples.text: One plays a neighbor. The other starts a gospel conversation and invites a next step.

examples.title: Role-play a hesitant friend
examples.text: One plays a friend who says, “I’m not religious.” The other listens, shares and invites kindly.

examples.title: Plan a real contact
examples.text: Each learner names one person to reach out to this week and what they will say.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand finding people to teach? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in a few minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Testify that the Lord prepares people and asks us to help find them. Invite learners to share a time they felt prompted to reach out.

tips.text: Ask learners to read one scripture each and share what it promises.
Let learners write down what they plan to do.
Help learners feel free to say they feel nervous. Then show them a simple first step.
Tell a story, then ask what it teaches.

quote.text: The worth of souls is great in the sight of God.

study: Read Doctrine and Covenants 100:5–6 together and ask what the Lord promises when we open our mouths.
invitations: Finish the plan you wrote in class for how you will help someone learn about the gospel.
Look through the contacts on your phone. Reach out to a friend or a less-active member.
Explore the Church’s website for videos and ideas to share.
Share a video from the Church with a friend and tell them how it made you feel.
